initial_prompt: What's the difference between crocodiles and alligators?

messages.content: What's the difference between crocodiles and alligators?

The easiest way to tell them apart is the snout shape—alligators have wide, U-shaped snouts while crocodiles have longer, V-shaped ones. When their mouths are closed, you can see a crocodile's fourth tooth sticking out on the bottom jaw, but an alligator's teeth are hidden. Crocodiles also tend to be more aggressive and can tolerate saltwater better than alligators, which prefer freshwater. In the wild, alligators live mainly in the southeastern US and China, while crocodiles have a much broader range across tropical regions.
